title: Units Asked For on a Prior Authorization Extension Request
content:
In Prairie Ridge Prior Authorization, the units an extension request asks for are the class's weekly frequency cap multiplied by the whole weeks of the class's extension days, less the units remaining on the authorization, never below zero. The whole weeks of the extension days are the extension days divided by seven and rounded down. In a class that sets no weekly frequency cap, the units an extension request asks for are the class's extension allotment.

The weekly frequency cap, the extension days and the extension allotment are the figures of the authorization's Prior Authorization class; a weekly frequency cap of zero means the class sets no weekly cap. The units remaining are the units-remaining balance shown on the authorization on the day of the request.

## The calculation in parts

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| Whole weeks | the class's extension days divided by seven, rounded down to a whole number |
| Units for the weeks | the class's weekly frequency cap multiplied by the whole weeks |
| Units asked for | the units for the weeks less the units remaining on the authorization |
| Floor | a figure below zero is taken as zero |
| Class with no weekly cap | the units asked for are the class's extension allotment |

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

- A class with a weekly frequency cap of 3 units and 60 extension days: sixty divided by seven is eight and four sevenths, so eight whole weeks; three multiplied by eight is 24 units. With 5 units remaining on the authorization, the request asks for 24 less 5, that is 19 units.
- The same class with 30 units remaining: 24 less 30 falls below zero, so the request asks for 0 units.
- A class with a weekly frequency cap of 5 units and 14 extension days: two whole weeks, 10 units; with no units remaining the request asks for 10 units.
- A class whose weekly frequency cap is zero and whose extension allotment is 13 units: the request asks for 13 units, whatever the units remaining.
